title: 2002 HMMT February Guts Problem 44
statement:
The unknown real numbers \(x, y, z\) satisfy the equations

\[\frac{x+y}{1+z}=\frac{1-z+z^{2}}{x^{2}-x y+y^{2}} ; \quad \frac{x-y}{3-z}=\frac{9+3 z+z^{2}}{x^{2}+x y+y^{2}}\]

Find \(x\).

solutions.text: \(\sqrt[3]{14}\) Cross-multiplying in both equations, we get, respectively, \(x^{3}+y^{3}=\) \(1+z^{3}, x^{3}-y^{3}=27-z^{3}\). Now adding gives \(2 x^{3}=28\), or \(x=\sqrt[3]{14}\).
